citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility does not use appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries for the
following animals:
“Archie” a male lamb was diagnosed with a degloved tail injury on May 27, 2026. The lamb was treated at the Attending
Veterinarian’s (AV) clinic and sent back with “at home” care instructions. The AV recommended docking the lamb’s tail if it
was unable to heal medically. On June 23, 2026, the facility reached out to the AV to schedule a tail amputation for Archie
and to address intermittent coughing from a group of animals; “Belle” a cow; “Solo” and “Marilyn” two sheep; “Ma”,
“Trouble”, “Bullet”, and “Daiquiri” four goats. The AV responded by requesting that the facility call to schedule a visit to
address the concerns. The facility did not follow through to schedule the tail amputation for Archie or to address the
intermittent coughing for the group of animals. At the time of the inspection, the USDA inspector observed a dime-sized
scabbed area at the tip of Archie’s tail.
“Peaches” a female lamb was diagnosed with a degloved tail injury on July 29, 2026, through photo documentation by the
facility staff provided to the AV. The facility informed the AV of the injury but did not schedule an appointment to have the
animal evaluated or treated by the AV. At the time of the inspection, the USDA inspector observed approximately 1 inch of
the end of the tail devoid of skin, hair or flesh. The area was caked in dirt.
Failure to use the appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries can lead to delayed
healing times, injuries and/or worsening of symptoms for the animals. Correct by maintaining a program of adequate
veterinary care that uses the appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries.
Correct by August 18, 2026.

The facility’s current natural shelter for one adult male dromedary camel is not appropriate for the local climate conditions.
Both the primary and secondary enclosures for the camel provide limited protection from heavy downpours through the
use of natural plant life [trees and shrubbery]. The lack of appropriate natural or artificial shelter may lead to injury or
discomfort from local climatic conditions. Correct by providing natural or artificial shelter appropriate to the local climatic
conditions for the camel.
Temporary correction completed by the time of the exit interview.
Permanent correction due by August 31, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with ______.
